title: A2v10 metadata.json (state)
description: One set of states: the life cycle of an entity, as a closed list of codes each carrying a colour and a role. An enum plus those two, and the two are why it is a kind of its own - a column pointing here says the record HAS a life cycle. Named after the ENTITY whose states these are: 'state/order'. The baseline is the platform's (Id, Name, Memo, Order, Void, Color, Role); 'fields' adds the author's own columns, which every state fills by name and which travel with every reference to the set. No forms, no rules. Transitions are not declared yet.

description.description: For the model, not the platform: nothing reads it - no generator, runtime or deploy. Where the model writes down what it must know about this endpoint - its rules and the reasons for them - so the next session finds them here.

table.description: The SQL table of the set, in schema 'state'. Declared and never derived from the folder - the same rule every other endpoint follows.

model.description: Base of the generated names: the row type ('T' + model), the array (its plural) and the localization keys of the values. Defaults to the folder name in PascalCase plus 'State' - 'order' gives 'OrderState' - because the entity's own word already names its records.

fields.description: The author's own columns of a state, next to the baseline. Each state fills them under the column's name; they ride with every reference to the set.

values.description: The states, in the order they are shown - 'order' is the position here and is never written. The list is the whole truth about the set: a state dropped from it is marked void on deploy, never deleted, so the records that carry it keep it and it merely stops being offered. The 'All' row a filter shows is not declared here - the platform adds it, with the empty string for a key and no role.

items.description: Any key besides the ones below is a column of 'fields', spelled as the column, with a scalar value. A column the state does not name is left as the deploy found it. A key that is no column fails the load.

id.description: The code, as the referencing column stores it.

name.description: Presentation. Defaults to the localization key '@[{model}.{id}]'. The key carries the set's name on purpose: two equal codes in two sets would otherwise collapse into one translation, and that does not surface until the second language.

color.description: How the state is drawn - a badge in the grid, a coloured item in the picker. Lower case: the value goes straight into a CSS class, where case matters. Optional; without one the state draws as a plain label. A colour named 'success' is not the role of that name.

role.description: What this state is to the cycle, spelled exactly as it is stored. 'Initial' - a new record starts here; exactly one state is it. 'InProgress' - the cycle is under way; any number. 'Success' - it reached its goal; exactly one state is it. 'Failure' - it ended without reaching the goal; any number, and none of them means a technical error. Nothing else is declared: 'is it over' is Success or Failure, 'is it still open' is Initial or InProgress.

void.description: Withdrawn from use: stays in the records that already carry it and leaves the list of candidates. A record holding a void state opens with an empty control and cannot be saved until a live one is picked - which is the intended migration, not a defect. Void states are not counted when the platform checks for exactly one 'Initial' and one 'Success'.
